title: Saving today for later years
summary: Retirement savings like NPS are for long-term goals, with rules about when you can use them.

variants.markdown:
**English draft for R5 review.**

Anil is 25 and his father, Mr Rao, retired last year. Mr Rao says, "I wish I had started saving for these years earlier."

**Retirement** is the stage of life when you stop working for income, so savings must cover your needs. The **National Pension System (NPS)** is a government-backed scheme where people put money in regularly until they are older.

Starting early helps because money has more years to grow. In this example, assume ₹2,000 a month at an assumed 8% a year for 35 years. That is an assumption for this example, not a promise, as real results differ.

NPS has **lock-in rules**: most of the money cannot be taken out until a set age, with limited early exits. That protects the goal but means it is not for everyday spending.

Gullak teaches how it works. It does not tell anyone what to choose.

Gullak uses virtual play money only.

questions.prompt: What is retirement savings meant for?

options.text: Meeting your needs after you stop earning

questions.explanation: Retirement savings are for the years when regular income stops.

questions.prompt: Why does starting early usually help?

options.text: Money has more years to grow

questions.explanation: More time lets growth build on itself, though any rate in an example is only an assumption.

questions.prompt: What does a lock-in rule in NPS mean?

options.text: You can withdraw anything any day
Money is only for people under 18
Most money cannot be taken out until a set age

questions.explanation: Lock-in rules protect the long-term goal by limiting early withdrawals.
